outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.reason: ServiceNow (+7.4%) and Adobe (+6.1%) posted sharp bounces off their post-earnings and downgrade-driven declines, while Salesforce extended its recovery from Morgan Stanley's downgrade-driven drop — a notably strong stretch for the group after weeks of pressure.

strongest.area: Chip-equipment names with structural demand (ASML) and AI hardware picks-and-shovels
strongest.reason: ASML remains one of the few chip names higher this week after raising its full-year 2026 revenue outlook for the second time this year on AI-driven demand, while Cadence and Vishay Precision Group also bounced, even as the broader memory-chip complex sold off hard.

weakest.area: Memory chips & AI hardware supply chain
weakest.reason: A Korea-led KOSPI selloff (SK Hynix, Samsung both down sharply) dragged U.S. memory names lower — Micron fell roughly 6% to $929 and SanDisk dropped about 9% — while Arm remains down over 8% from its post-earnings drop despite a record quarter, as supply-constraint concerns weigh on sentiment ahead of SK Hynix's July 29 earnings.

The Nasdaq closed a volatile week near a one-month low as investors kept scrutinizing AI-capex guidance versus near-term returns; Oracle remains the weakest of the group, still working through the same capex-return debate as its megacap cloud peers.

outlook.nextStep: The July 28-29 Fed meeting is the single biggest catalyst on the calendar — markets currently price roughly a two-thirds chance of no change, but oil-driven inflation worries have pushed the 10-year yield to its highest since January 2025, so this is worth watching closely rather than acting on ahead of time. The enterprise-software bounce (ServiceNow, Adobe, Salesforce) and ASML's second guidance raise this year look like the more durable, multi-day signals worth a closer look; the Korea-led memory rout is a sharper, single-catalyst move better watched for confirmation, especially with Teradyne and SK Hynix earnings both landing this week.

signals.title: Fed meeting July 28-29 is the market's next big catalyst
signals.body: The Fed's July 28-29 meeting (decision Wednesday at 2pm ET) is one of the four 2026 meetings without a Summary of Economic Projections, so there's no fresh dot plot. CME FedWatch-style pricing currently shows roughly a 65% chance of no change, with expectations for a possible move shifting toward the September meeting. Oil-driven inflation worries have pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since January 2025.
signals.watch: Any inflation data or Fed commentary before Wednesday, and whether oil prices keep climbing on geopolitical risk.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a binary policy event just days away could move markets sharply in either direction.

signals.title: Korea-led memory chip selloff extends into a second week
signals.body: An overnight KOSPI selloff led by SK Hynix and Samsung spread again to U.S. memory names: Micron fell roughly 6% to about $929 and SanDisk dropped around 9%. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 1% on the move, extending a third straight losing session for the broader index. SK Hynix reports earnings on July 29, and pre-print positioning may be adding to the pressure.
signals.watch: Whether the selloff extends past SK Hynix's July 29 earnings, and whether other memory-adjacent names (Western Digital, Lam Research) follow the same pattern.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — this is a specific, sourced catalyst (Korea market weakness plus an upcoming earnings print) rather than vague sentiment.

signals.title: ServiceNow and Adobe post sharp rebounds
signals.body: ServiceNow rose roughly 7% and Adobe roughly 6% as both continued recovering from recent post-earnings and downgrade-driven declines, while Salesforce extended its own bounce off Morgan Stanley's downgrade-driven selloff earlier in the week.
signals.watch: Whether the bounce holds into next week, and whether analysts revisit the Adobe downgrade given the size of the rebound.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a rebound of this size across three names in the same group is a clearer signal than a single-stock move.

signals.title: Tesla says over 1,000 Optimus units now working inside Gigafactory Texas
signals.body: Tesla confirmed more than 1,000 Optimus humanoid robots are now sorting parts, carrying components, and performing quality inspections at Gigafactory Texas, with Optimus V3 production slated to begin this summer. Intuitive Surgical, meanwhile, is recovering part of last week's post-earnings plunge, when shares fell as much as ~14% intraday despite an EPS beat, on cautious procedure-growth guidance.
signals.watch: Confirmation of Optimus V3's production start this summer, and whether Intuitive Surgical's bounce holds as the market digests its guidance.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — the Optimus deployment numbers are a concrete, verifiable data point rather than a roadmap promise.

signals.title: Bitcoin holds near $64.5K over the weekend while Ethereum lags on exploit reports
signals.body: Bitcoin is holding close to $64,500, largely decoupled from the tech-driven equity selloff. Ethereum has underperformed, with reports of roughly $35M in losses from Ethereum-linked exploits compounding macro-driven weakness as it failed to reclaim the $2,000 level.
signals.watch: Whether Bitcoin's relative resilience continues if equity volatility picks up further, and any follow-up details on the reported Ethereum exploits.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — Bitcoin's continued decoupling from equities is a notable divergence, though the Ethereum exploit reports warrant some caution.

signals.title: Cybersecurity keeps outperforming broader enterprise software
signals.body: Palo Alto Networks and peers gained earlier in the week on analyst upgrades (including a Capital One Securities upgrade to Overweight), continuing a pattern where cybersecurity names have outperformed the broader enterprise-software group. CrowdStrike and Zscaler pulled back today even as the group's relative strength narrative holds.
signals.watch: Whether the cybersecurity-vs-software performance gap keeps widening, and any follow-through from the recent analyst upgrades.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a sector-wide relative-strength pattern like this tends to be more durable than any single day's move.

signals.title: Cadence and Synopsys bounce off AI-disruption fears
signals.body: Cadence and Synopsys both firmed up after last week's selloff tied to reports of a Chinese AI model designing a chip without proprietary EDA tools, though Synopsys remains lower on the day while Cadence has recovered further.
signals.watch: Any further reporting on AI-assisted chip design tools and whether it changes analysts' views on EDA-software moats.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — the underlying AI-disruption question for EDA software is still more narrative than confirmed impact.
